reconcile.note: Fausset reads John's cannot sin as describing the regenerate nature's incompatibility with sin, not a denial that believers still commit and confess individual sins.

discrepancy.note: Remsburg juxtaposes the Johannine claim that the God-born cannot sin against the Bible's own repeated verdict that no one is sinless.

quotes.text: How are Christ’s true followers to be distinguished from those of the devil? “Whosoever is born of God doth not commit sin” (1 John iii, 9). “He that committeth sin is of the devil” (8).
quotes.attr: John E. Remsburg (d. 1919), The Christ: A Critical Review and Analysis of the Evidences of His Existence (1909), "How are Christ's true followers to be distinguished from those of the devil?", on 1 John 3:8-9.

quotes.text: Judged by this standard what is the comparative strength of these sovereigns’ subjects? “There is no man that sinneth not” (1 Kings viii, 46).
quotes.attr: John E. Remsburg (d. 1919), The Christ: A Critical Review and Analysis of the Evidences of His Existence (1909), on 1 Kings 8:46.

quotes.text: “There is not a just man upon earth” (Ecclesiastes vii, 20).
quotes.attr: John E. Remsburg (d. 1919), The Christ: A Critical Review and Analysis of the Evidences of His Existence (1909), on Ecclesiastes 7:20.

sides.snippet: If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves
sides.verseText: If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.

sides.snippet: he can't sin, because he is born of God
sides.verseText: Whoever is born of God doesn't commit sin, because his seed remains in him; and he can't sin, because he is born of God.
